maybe ted was a revolutionary? ironic he would advocate separating from human nature like that.

>It is hard to imagine that a mammal could engage in extensive surrogate activities WITHOUT a fairly complex use of symbolic thought/language, just like it is hard to imagine a TOTAL absence of surrogate activities if a mamal has language and muh opposing thumbs.
It was bound to happen, but it's gone completely off the fucking rails, surely you must see this....

we are superior to other animals. what other animal has the prospect to become a literal god through gene editing? and why should we lower ourselves to the level of other animals? nature will always return in the end, why not use the potential of the only animal that has figured out the inner workings of the world rather than been its hopeless captive? to me surrogate activities are necessary. the problem of depression seems to be mostly one of a lack of meaning, which itself is entirely subjective, making it a surrogate activity. I remember hearing somewhere that after a European explorer met a native tribesmen from somewhere in the world, the tribesman had lost the confidence in his religion and committed suicide. his, and our salvation lay, imo, in the surrogate activity of constructing a subjective worldview. I think as long as we have this, spending all of our energy on hunting won't be necessary to maintaining our happiness.

Was going through ISAIF real quick and came across an interesting point that actually supports your thesis or whatever that oversocialization was NOT exclusively a modern phenomenon:

>One of the most important means by which our society socializes children is by making them feel ashamed of behavior or speech that is contrary to society’s expectations. If this is overdone, or if a particular child is especially susceptible to such feelings, he ends by feeling ashamed of HIMSELF. 

Shame has been around for ages. Even Freud addressed this in his works. Whether Freud can be trusted or not is a different matter, but in any case, he went into some depth into the role shame plays in the education of very small children. 

Problem with the quote above from ISAIF is that Ted doesn't come out and openly state that shame is a new OR an old phenomenon. 
Given his inordinately high intelligence, it's probably safe to assume that he is probably being purposely ambiguous on this point.

>our ability to experience life while being self aware has led to us to become nihilitic and to question everything unless we somehow occupy our minds with whatever meaning we convince ourselves is ultimate. this inherent religiosity is unseparable from tribal cultures yet is it not also a surrogate activity? it seems like these kinds of surrogate activities are inherent in our nature because of our ability to be self aware and our need to restrict that lest we question too much about the universe.

This is also good point. 
Language has a whole lot to do with this as well, obviously. 
It is hard to imagine that a mammal could engage in extensive surrogate activities WITHOUT a fairly complex use of symbolic thought/language, just like it is hard to imagine a TOTAL absence of surrogate activities if a mamal has language and muh opposing thumbs.
It was bound to happen, but it's gone completely off the fucking rails, surely you must see this...."}]
